financial_checks.claim: Roth IRA goal: max out $7,500 this year; $4,100 in so far; automated $200 a paycheck
financial_checks.result: $200 x 24-26 paychecks = $4,800-$5,200 a year, below $7,500. $4,100 is 20.5 paychecks at $200; if that many have run, $3,400 remaining needs about $570-$970 per remaining paycheck (4-6 remaining). The goal cannot be met at $200 a paycheck.

financial_checks.claim: Emergency fund of $9,200 built "$200 at a time" over 15 months
financial_checks.result: $6,000-$6,500 at $200 per paycheck; $9,200 implies other deposits. $9,200 / 6 months is $1,533 a month of coverage.

financial_checks.claim: FTC: more than 1.3 million identity theft reports and fraud losses over $15.8 billion
financial_checks.result: FTC 2025 fraud losses were $15.9 billion (3 million reports) per search summaries (2024: about $12.5 billion); the 1.3 million identity-theft count was not located; "this year" refers to a full prior year.

financial_checks.claim: IRS 2026 limits: 401(k) $24,500; IRA $7,500; estate exemption $15 million; annual gift exclusion $19,000
financial_checks.result: Matches the published 2026 limits as recalled by the analyst; not re-fetched.

financial_checks.claim: UNC Criminal Justice study: more than 75% of convicted burglars use social media and Google Street View; Allstate: one in three post vacation plans, closer to one in two for your age
financial_checks.result: The UNC study was not located: a 50-person UK ex-burglar survey reports 74% (Street View) and 78% (social media), and the Allstate figures are from a 2025 Canadian survey (32% overall; 51% of ages 18-34). The attribution is unverified.

financial_checks.result: Not re-verified; the half-of-Americans figure is in line with Bankrate-type surveys.

strengths: Distinctive second-person narrative form and unusually strong recurring characters.
Clear numbered structure matching the title.
Specific protective actions (credit freeze, alerts, delayed posting).
weaknesses: The stated Roth automation cannot reach its goal; the savings balance implies unstated deposits.
Causal claims linking disclosure to fraud are asserted.
Thumbnail scene is not in the script; no visible ask in the stored text.
contradictions: $200 per paycheck cannot reach the $7,500 Roth goal by December.
"Don't tell anyone" versus telling Kayla where the documents live.
Burglar study attribution versus the UK survey found.
Looking poor (thumbnail) versus "looking poor isn't the same as being safe" (opening).
improvement_opportunities: Change the Roth line to "$625 a month" or "$4,100 so far and $3,400 to go" so the arithmetic matches.
Replace the burglar-study claim with a named, checkable study and state the sample.
Put the supermarket scene in the script or change the thumbnail to the coffee-shop opening.
Say "seven things" aloud in the first 30 seconds and list them in order.
Add a closing ask tied to the content (freeze your credit with the three bureaus tonight).
